results.fact: Round-trip / total hiking distance
results.evidence: Published round-trip figures for the Barclay/Tailgunner line disagree widely: two GPS trip reports give 5.44 mi and 5.5 mi (matching the row's 2.75 mi one-way waypoint), while the WTA hike stats and a detailed hiker blog give 7.5 mi, AllTrails 7.2 mi, another guide 6.5 mi and a two-day report 6 mi. No figure has clear independent agreement over the others, so the itinerary's 7.5 mi was not changed.

results.fact: Rope length needed
results.correct_value: A 30 m rope is sufficient (optional handline / one short rappel at the hidden ramp)
results.evidence: A WTA trip report says the only roped spot is the ~10 ft hidden-ramp step and that a 30 m rope was ample as a handline; a two-day trip report describes the descent as one short rappel over the hidden ramp, and another report notes a rappel station above that single step. Nothing on the route calls for a 50-60 m rope, so detailed_rack now matches rope_length_m and descent_text.

patches.find: A 50-60 meter rope is optional but recommended for groups with inexperienced members or for emergency descents.
patches.replace: A 30 m rope is optional but recommended for groups with inexperienced members, as a handline or for the one short rappel at the hidden ramp.

results.fact: Named route line on the face
results.evidence: 'Gunn Peak via Tailgunner Pass - South Face - East Ridge' is the name a detailed trip report uses for this same standard line: it climbs the south face (hidden ramp) to the notch east of the summit and finishes along the east ridge/north-side ledges, which is what climbing_route describes; Gunn Point is a named 5,760 ft point beside Gunn Basin passed on the approach. The face label and the prose describe the same line.

results.fact: Total elevation gain (gain_ft/loss_ft 4,700 vs itinerary gainFt/lossFt and totalNote 4,900)
results.evidence: gain_ft says 4,700 while the itinerary says 4,900. Sources scatter: 4,700 (two-day trip report), 4,900 (WTA hike stats), 4,380, 4,300, 4,105 and 4,060 (other reports/guides). Net rise trailhead-to-summit is about 4,050 ft. No value has clear independent agreement, so nothing was changed.

results.fact: Which approach/line this route actually follows
results.evidence: Sources agree the 1915 first ascent went via Lewis Creek, and a USGS-named Lewis Creek lies near Index, a different drainage from Barclay Creek. But no source found gives any modern beta for a Lewis Creek line. The row's approach, descent, pitch_detail, approach_variants and waypoints all describe the Barclay Creek/Tailgunner Pass/hidden-ramp standard route, while the itinerary and timing notes call it a separate, unmarked north/west-side line. The overview calls it 'essentially the same corridor'. Deciding whether this row is a duplicate of the Southeast Route or a real separate line needs a product decision or new beta; nothing was changed.

results.fact: Which route the 1915 first ascent followed
results.evidence: The Southeast Route overview states the 1915 party and date as a fact about the peak, then begins a separate sentence describing the modern standard route; it never says the 1915 party climbed that line. This route's fa ('via Lewis Creek') fits that reading.

results.fact: Whether the route reaches a summit
results.evidence: The 'Guye Peak' waypoint is the peak's own summit, labelled with the peak's name and given no distance along the route. It works as a landmark and for the summit weather. Overview, descent_text and watch_out all say plainly that the route does not top out, which matches the route's listing (bolts, #1 Camalot, 2-bolt chain anchor, no top-out). Waypoint type/position is out of scope.

results.fact: Elevation gain for the route
results.evidence: The approach is described as about half a mile and 15 minutes from the Alpental lot, whose ground elevation is about 3,127 ft (USGS 3DEP point query). But the stored crag pin sits on ground at about 4,227 ft (USGS query), which would fit the 1,200 ft gain, while the crag waypoint's own elev says 3,400. No source gives the crag's elevation, so the right gain cannot be set; the pin, the waypoint elev and gain_ft need checking against each other.

results.fact: Which trailhead/approach this route uses
results.correct_value: Unsigned Cave Ridge/Snoqualmie Mountain climbers' path from the Snow Lake trailhead to the Cave Ridge-Guye saddle, then class 3 north to the north summit
results.evidence: SummitPost's 'North Route "Hidden Ridge"' page describes parking at Alpental, starting up the Cave Ridge/Snoqualmie 'trail' about 100 ft south of the Snow Lake Trail, climbing to the Cave Ridge-Guye saddle and turning right to the north summit (class 3 in summer). WTA's Guye Peak entry describes the same steep climbers' trail shared with Snoqualmie Mountain and Cave Ridge (3.0 mi RT, 2,000 ft). The itinerary day and timing note had been copied from the West Face talus approach and a 'North Rib' climb, and now describe this route. Hours, miles and gain were left unchanged because they already match.

results.fact: Location, grade and structure of the route's crux
results.evidence: This row mixes two different routes. The Mountaineers' Guye Peak/West Face is the big tree-covered ramp across the face with a ~40 ft class 4-low 5th step, which is what beta and the itinerary describe. Mountain Project's Improbable Traverse (5.8, 6 pitches, Grade III, FA Hiser/Borghoff 1960) is what rock_grade, pitch_detail and this row's fa describe, and that route already has its own row (wa_guye_peak_improbable_traverse). Fixing this means deciding which route the row is and rewriting the other half, so nothing was changed.
